subject: Proposal: usage offset & short-term SLA amendment after Feb 10 latency window
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@luminahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumina Health SRE <sre@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spike impacting inference pipeline

Hi Monica,

We saw a sustained latency increase across our production inference endpoints between 03:14–03:52 UTC this morning. P50 went from ~45ms to ~620ms and P95 spiked above 1.2s. This caused backpressure in our queuing layer and a downstream retry storm that touched multiple services.

We have attached a short incident export with traces and timestamps — the SREs flagged a model routing fallback that appears correlated to the incident. Lumina is running this in a pilot for clinical triage, so any downtime/latency has real product impact.

We'd like to request:
- A formal incident timeline from Redwood
- A short-term remediation (e.g., configuration change or model variant) so this doesn't reoccur this week
- Compensation for the affected window — usage credit or a one-time credit to offset the incident impact while we evaluate longer-term mitigations

Can you confirm next steps? We are prioritizing stability over new features right now.

Thanks,
Ellen
Senior Platform Engineer
Lumina Health

Attachment: latency-incident-log-20260210.csv

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Lumina Health SRE <sre@luminahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spike impacting inference pipeline

Hi Ellen —

I'm really sorry this happened — thank you for the incident export, that helps a lot. Short answers up front:
1) We're already investigating; our routing team saw an automatic fallback trigger on the inference cluster during that window.
2) Immediate mitigation: I can push a model-variant pin for your routes to avoid the fallback, and we can roll that out safely in the next 60 minutes (pending your sign-off).
3) Compensation: we are prepared to offer a usage offset for the affected billing period — my proposal is a one-time credit equal to the measured token usage during the impacted window plus an additional 10% goodwill buffer.

I'll escalate to my leadership to get formal approval for that credit and to legal for a short amendment that documents the one-time offset and a brief SLA clarification about routing fallbacks. I will follow up with a concrete dollar/credit amount in the next 24 hours.

Would you like us to proceed with the model-variant pin now?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
mobile: (415) 555-0198

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Exec approval for one-time usage offset + short amendment (Lumina Health, DL-7421)

Team —

Lumina Health (pilot customer, clinical triage) reported a latency incident on 2026-02-10 that materially impacted their production traffic for ~38 minutes. The customer provided traces (attached in the customer thread). I spoke to them and proposed a one-time usage offset equal to measured tokens during the window + 10% goodwill as a stopgap while we finalize the routing fix. They also want the routing fallback behavior clarified in a short amendment (no change to standard SLA, just documentation for this case and a clause that enables a one-time offset).

Why this matters:
- Strategic: Lumina is in a paid pilot with potential to expand to multiple hospitals (high strategic ARR upside).
- Risk: If we don't move fast here they may pause their pilot and delay procurement cycles.
- Precedent: This is not a systemic platform outage (no multi-customer downtime), but the customer impact is business-critical for them. We should treat this as an escalation where a small commercial concession is warranted.

Proposed commercial terms for approval:
- One-time usage credit = token-usage-during-window * price-per-token (estimated $3,120) + 10% goodwill => proposed credit $3,432 (rounded).
- Additionally, offer a complimentary one month of Standard support for the pilot period (not a recurring credit).
- Condition: Customer signs a 30-day amendment acknowledging the incident timeline and accepting the model-variant pin as the immediate mitigation. Amendment to be drafted by Legal (I've linked a draft).

Requesting:
- Marissa: approve the $3.4k one-time credit under your sign-off authority?
- Vivek: if you prefer different optics (e.g., convert part of this to a one-time invoice discount vs. platform credit) let me know — customer prefers a platform credit applied to the next invoice.
- Rishi/Legal: quick review of the short amendment draft (attached link) — can we expedite DocuSign?

Attachments: incident export (from customer), preliminary cost calc, amendment draft link.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call if helpful.

Thanks —
Monica

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for one-time usage offset + short amendment (Lumina Health, DL-7421)

Monica — thanks for the clear write-up. I approve the proposed concession with a minor tweak:
- Approve up to $3,500 one-time platform credit (applied to next invoice) rather than a manual refund.
- Approve one complimentary month of Standard support for the pilot window.
- Legal to review and send the 30-day amendment; the amendment must include language that the credit is a one-time remediation and does not set precedent for SLA changes.

Marissa — you have approval authority; please confirm and coordinate the ledger entry so Finance applies the credit cleanly against DL-7421. Rishi — please fast-track legal review & DocuSign. Monica — you may communicate approved terms to Lumina and implement the model-variant pin once Lumina confirms.

Vivek

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Lumina Health SRE <sre@luminahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency spike impacting inference pipeline

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the incident export and for your patience while we reviewed the event. Internal updates:
- We will pin your routes to the stable model variant now; our infra team validated the change in staging and we will deploy the pin at 10:15 PST today after your confirmation. This should prevent the automatic fallback observed in your traces.
- Executive approval: Redwood will apply a one-time platform credit of $3,432 (we rounded to $3,400 internally and Vivek has authorized up to $3,500) to your next invoice for DL-7421. This credit covers measured usage during the impacted window plus a 10% goodwill buffer.
- We will also add one complimentary month of Standard support for the pilot period.
- Legal will send a short 30-day amendment to the existing MSA that documents this remediation and clarifies routing fallback behavior; signing the amendment is a condition for the credit.

Next steps for you: please reply with a quick OK to the model pin and confirm you will sign the amendment when it arrives. Once we have that, we will finalize the credit and confirm ledger entries.

Apologies again for the disruption — we understand the sensitivity here and are committed to making this right quickly.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-amendment-draft.pdf
